notes.title: The Gun Update 1
notes.notes:
Hello folks!

It is I, Van Hohlsinn. And I bring you todays update.



It comes with 2 new guns that you can find throughout the run and some changes and improvements to the game.



Lets take a look!


The new weapons
The Arc Welder

A gun that can be found in deeper dive levels that will zap its projectiles through multiple enemies and cause damage this way. It is perfect to lighten dense crowds of enemies.



The Boomer

Which does not mean that I added a person or something. It's another gun. And I kind of made it just for me. Because I can't aim, you see. And with this gun - I don't need to aim.

In fact, it is a lot better to shoot anywhere but at the enemy.

Projectiles will bounce off walls and hit enemies this way. The damage will increase with each bounce, if you can manage to land hits after multiple bounces!

Bounced projectiles also will knock back enemies.


Gameplay changes
Peristent weapons

Weapons will now stay with you in between dive levels.

So when entering a deeper level, you don't have to collect all weapons again. Which should make early scavenger encounters a lot more manageable. But it also feels a whole lot less annoying.



Improved Loot drop strats

Some loot items are now locked by dive level.

This mostly pertains to weapons. So you will not find the biggest and baddest weapons early on, you will have to look deeper down for them!



Shield items are now also locked by player health. So they will not drop when you're full health.

Which seems minor but it never felt right to collect shields when you stand to gain nothign from them.



Improvements to Little Clankers Ram ability 

The ram ability will now grant speed boost when active. It will deal more damage and it will knock back enemies. Knocked back enemies that hit walls will take damage from the impact.

Visual upgrades have been made as well.


Little things
Improved the auto-level code, feels much better now

Minimap controls will now adhere to the auto leveling options

Moved Little Clankers cockpit around some for a bit more view. Might need some more work yet

Added health bars to most things that are shootable

Added damage indicators

Fixed world gen lagging behind one dive level when sampling for max generation size.



And that concludes todays update!



I hope you enjoy the new stuff. There is more to come, yet!



Cheers!

notes.title: The Tactical Update Part 4
notes.notes:
Hello and welcome!

Today I'm bringing you the last part of the Tactical Update. Lets see what I have this time.


Unlockable ships
The demo comes with one unlockable ship. The Little Clanker. It's a heavy ship and plays and feels very different from Mothrust or the Junker.

By diving deeper into the levels, you can encounter enemy scavengers and get parts to build Little Clanker from.


Ship Abilities
Ships have special abilities now.

They can be toggled on and off using the F key on your keyboard or the Y key on your XInput compatible controller. Or whichever key you might want to map this to.

Mothrust now has the ability to use a nitrous boost to become insanely fast.

Little Clanker has the ability to ram into things and damage them.

Anything you can shoot, you can ram.


Technical Notes
If you have played the demo already, you will probably need to go into the control scheme options and check that the "Toggle Ship Ability" is bound. I recommend the F key on keyboard or Y on an XInput controller.



This update concludes the Tactical Update.

It has been quite a journey from February to June. Thanks for sticking around and stay tuned!

I'm sure there's more to come.

notes.title: The Tactical Update Part 3
notes.notes:
Hello again!

It's time for the 3rd part of the tactical update. This time around I have balancing changes and a more rounded dive experience for you.
Lets have a look.

New Runs:
I have changed the way, runs work.
There is now a notable progression in each of them, that should make it easier to find your way around and make a more informed decision if you want to keep diving deeper or leave the run with what you got.

The "rare artifacts" - also known as temporal damping units - have been repurposed.
You still collect them from cracking flesh boxes and clearing rooms. (More activities in the future!)
Now you will need them to be able to dive into deeper levels of the anomaly.
With each level, the map will become more complex and the enemies plenty.

In a future update, these deep levels will be the place to hunt for new ships!
I know. It seems like a fairly important feature. And it will come. But it felt important to me to drop the new update now. Because ...

... of the balancing changes:
Enemy damage has been toned down slightly to account for the player damage that has been toned down overall. This was necessary for a number of reasons.
But most importantly, I wanted you to feel the impact of the various damage mod opportunities. 

There are some ship mods you can equip, that made no noticable difference to your combat because the base damage output was already pretty high.

Now taking ship mods along that cause damage output changes is a viable and meaningful decision.
I have also changed how Weapon Overdrive works.
Instead of crippling your base damage as a trade-off for boosting damage pickups, the capacity of damage pickups is drastically reduced instead.
So you get a LOT of firepower. Only for a limited amount of shots. But you will not need to sacrifice your base damage output anymore.

Lastly, the weapons got their unique feel and reason for existence back. You'll see.

Alright. And for good measure, I threw in a new post-run screen.
You can earn badges now. See what you can get!

Know Issues:
* Some transit elements currently can appear at the end of the map and they are not shut off.
	* You can exit the map, break your immersion and possibly experience some funky rendering shenanigans this way. I'm working on fixing the generator to prevent such generations from happening.
	* Meanwhile, if you're into behind-the-scenes sillyness, go ahead and enjoy the breakage. Otherwise, just turn around, the generated map is still 100% operational.

And that's it for this update.
I hope you'll enjoy it!

Cheers

notes.title: The Tactical Update - Part 2
notes.notes:
Hello again, folks!

Today is the day for a new demo update!
It is another step towards finishing the Tactical Update. It also seems like the game is taking a turn in the rougelike direction. But see for yourself.

This update, in particular, brings a revamped AI, rebalanced loot drops, a new pre-dive UI, new enemy units and more.


Here, have a changelog:


Improved enemy ai

	They will make an effort not to shoot through walls
	They will get stuck a lot less
	Units now organise themselfes in squads and share targets and squad leader locations
	New internal AI logic (it plays about the same but I can sleep better at night, now)

New enemy types

	Factory units (they spawn support drones for their squad)
	Shield Leech units (they steal your shield and transfer it to a squad member)
	Tank units (they fly in between you and their squad members)
	Infested units (they shoot infested ammunition that can temporarily cause defense debuffs)

New ship mods

	Reverse shield leeches (gain shield from enemy squads)
	Flesh Resonator (spread the infested defense debuff while being debuffed yourself)

Various improvements in enemy unit placements to make for tighter combat
Rebalanced loot drops:

	Weapons and mods can be found in loot crates
	Enemy units drop resources and shield pickups

Added option for anti aliasing
Improved pre-dive UI with better controller support
Unit and other object indicators (with option to turn them off)
Improved shotgun and pulsegun SFX
Improved flesh box task - now drops rare artifacts
Fix shield not getting correct starter-amount when capacity was modified
Old Rusty (now Mothrust) and the Haulin' Junk have different graphic for representation now


There are at the very least 2 more updates planned, that will introduce more variety within the dungeons and depth to the runs themselves.

Also, you will probably have guessed it at this point, you will be able to find new ships to fly in the future. Ships with their own set of properties to allow for unique builds together with the available ship mods.

But for now, what you see in this change log, is what we go with for this month.
I hope you'll enjoy checking out the new enemies and mods.

If you have any questions, absolutely drop them here or in the forum.
I'll be around, answering them!


Cheers!

notes.title: The Tactical Update - Part 1
notes.notes:
Hey folks!

I have been hard at work this past month to change the game around a little bit. I felt the pacing just wasn't right and the overall depth wasn't where I wanted it to be.

So I devised a plan, as one does in such scenario.

Turns out, it's so much that I can't put it all in one update if I don't want you to keep waiting for yet another month. So I decided to go and do this in parts! 

The whole thing is called The Tactical Update and aims to improve the depth of gameplay by adding support for different play styles and re-designing the gameplay loop to make anomaly diving more diversified and fun.

And that brings me to the contents of todays update. It lays the groundwork for all the things to come while also bringing something new to the game. Lets dive in.

Core Loop Changes
A dive into an Anomaly is now centered on getting as much loot out of there as you can possible get. With time, it will get harder and other scavengers might spawn in.

Likewise, you can now leave an anomaly at any time you feel like.
The minimap now shows indicators and names for what you find on the map. Exits are marked.
After a while, rooms that you have cleared will reset and you can visit them again.

Enemy spawning has been changed.
You will now have a lot less time to take a breath. These new anomaly dives can become pretty intense.

Resource Economy
Enemies will now drop certain resources in varying amounts. When you exit an anomaly successfully, you will get these resources to buy equipment for your ship.

Persistent Ships
The player ship is now persistent. That means, if it is destroyed in a run, you will have to repair it, before you can use it again.

In the event that you have no more resources to repair your ship - or other reasons why you don't want to bring your ship to an anomaly dive - there is a loaner ship. It's a bit of a junker though.

Loadout & Equipment
The ship now has three loadout slots. A shield and two Mod slots.
You can buy new equipment for the resources you have looted in previous anomaly dives.

Shields
You now have the option to equip different kinds of shields.
The demo comes with 3 different types for you to try. 
But of course, more are in the making.

Mods
These will alter some statistics about your ship. Mainly weapon damage, shield properties and speed.
Some mods might add new functionalities.
The demo comes with 4 mods for you to try out. Of course, here as well, more are in the making.

Other Stuff
Here are some more points that have changed in no particular order:

 Windowed mode option now works
 Added option to run borderless window
 Adjusted UI design to fit better with the pixel style
 Cockpit redesign
 Weapon selector now immediately switches weapons
 Controller: Shoulder buttons are now for banking
 Controller: A and X buttons are now for ascend and descend
 You may need to reset the controls in the options to get the new mapping. Or remap yourself.
 Damage balanacing
 Ammo display flashes when ammo is low
 Warning sound when ammo is low
 Feedback when shield is depleted and refilled
 Nerfed Quad Damage to Double Damage (this becomes quad damage with a certain ship mod equipped)


And that sums up this update.
Now that I look back, this kinda feels like a lot.
And you might wonder: What's next, then?

Honestly. It also depends on you.
The way I like my 6 DoF is different from the way you like yours and what the next guy was thinking.
Very much let me know what you would like to see added or improved!

Here are a couple of things I will definitely be working on.

I will probably replace pickups that get dropped from enemies with a different mechanic entirely. Won't spill yet what it is. But it will allow for more mods and loadout options. I think it's going to be amazing.
Of course, enemies will still drop loots. That's the entire point.

Different ships with different properties.

Well. This post is already taking enough of your time.
I said the important bits.
Time to get the latest update and check it out!
Leave me your feedback. Good, bad. I'll take it.

Cheers!

notes.title: Liha Patch 0.6.2
notes.notes:
Hello!

I received some feedback and, thank you!

Here comes an update to the demo that brings a couple things and fixes to make the game more enjoyable.

Didn't manage to squeeze everything in, that I think is important, but since this build contains a very important bugfix I wanted to get it out before the weekend.

Improvements:
* Fixed player receiving double damage 
* Resized Storage Room B
* Moved some spawn locations for infested lootbox guard drones to prevent them from getting stuck too much
* Opening minimap pauses game
* Ascending and descending now aligns to player instead of world orientation
* Added option to turn off auto-leveling the ship
* Added manual banking. Q and E by default, sensitivity adjustable via options
* Added FOV slider
* Via the options it is now possible to change the input bindings

And that's about it for this update!

On the roadmap (which will be also in the demo) is:

* Smarter AI
* More responsive weapon switching
* Shield-Break and Shield-Repair feedbacks
* More modifiers

Now you know.

With that being said, have a nice weekend, folks!
